headline: Lawrence mayor pleads not guilty to wiretap charges as council advances no-confidence vote
dek: Brian DePeña entered a not-guilty plea in Essex Superior Court and was released on personal recognizance; a council committee voted to send a no-confidence resolution to the full council.
body: Lawrence Mayor Brian DePeña pleaded not guilty Tuesday in Essex Superior Court to 14 counts of distributing a wiretapped communication and one count of witness intimidation. The arraignment in Salem moved the case from a grand-jury accusation into active state-court proceedings. [CBS Boston](https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/lawrence-massachusetts-mayor-brian-depena-wiretapping-arraignment/) reported that DePeña was released on personal recognizance and that his next hearing is scheduled for Dec. 9.

The charges stem from allegations first announced by the [Massachusetts Attorney General's Office](https://www.mass.gov/news/ags-office-announces-indictments-against-lawrence-mayor-for-wiretap-statute-violations-and-witness-intimidation). Prosecutors say DePeña asked for a private security system in his City Hall office, separate from the city's cameras, and that a hallway conversation between two municipal employees was captured on audio and video in March without at least one participant's knowledge. The attorney general's office said DePeña later distributed copies to 14 people. Those are allegations in the charging documents, not findings that he committed the offenses.

DePeña's lawyer, Neil Faigel, disputed the premise that the mayor controlled the system. In comments outside court reported by CBS Boston, Faigel said the cameras were installed by the city's information-technology department, that DePeña did not have passcodes and that he could not access the recordings. The defense position does not resolve the factual dispute; the state case will turn on evidence presented through the court process. DePeña did not answer questions about whether he would resign, according to the same report.

The court appearance coincided with a separate political response in Lawrence. The City Council's Committee of the Whole voted 5–2 to forward a no-confidence resolution to the full council, which is expected to take a final vote at its next regular meeting, [The Boston Globe reported](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/10/13/metro/lawrence-mayor-brain-depena-no-confidence/). The committee's action is symbolic: the council cannot force the mayor out through a no-confidence vote. Council President Jeovanny Rodriguez said the resolution concerns public trust and leadership, while opponents argued that a recall process would give residents the formal decision.

The council has also hired CliftonLarsonAllen for a comprehensive governance assessment, adding an administrative review to the criminal and political pressure surrounding City Hall. The Globe reported that DePeña intends to remain in office while the cases proceed. That means Lawrence residents are facing two separate questions: how the state prosecution develops, and how the mayor and council maintain day-to-day municipal services while the allegations remain unresolved.

The state case is separate from the federal case filed in August, in which prosecutors allege DePeña misused pandemic-relief loans for personal and campaign-related expenses. He has pleaded not guilty in that matter as well. The [Boston 25 report on Tuesday's arraignment](https://www.boston25news.com/news/local/lawrence-mayor-pleads-not-guilty-wiretapping-witness-intimidation-charges/ZSAVRE2E3VAC3IA6SZP3JJYCHQ/) said DePeña's attorney maintained that the mayor had no knowledge of how the City Hall cameras operated. Neither case has produced a conviction, and the next scheduled state-court date is the Dec. 9 hearing.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Lawrence mayor pleads not guilty as no-confidence vote advances
seoDescription: Brian DePeña pleaded not guilty to Massachusetts wiretap and witness-intimidation charges as Lawrence councilors advanced a no-confidence resolution.
